depends_on: Dirichlet/Mertens for progressions: sum of 1/p over primes = 9 mod 10 diverges
notes: If a prime p = 9 mod 10 divides n exactly once then 10 | sigma(n) (Lean: A065255_ten_dvd_sigma), so sigma(n) = n mod 10 iff 10 | n (A065255_iff); almost every n has such a prime, so B = {n : sigma(n) = n mod 10} has density 1/10 and b(k)/k -> 10. count.py: x/#B(x) = 9.979 at 3e6. Outside Lean: the density-zero step for n without such a prime (divergence of sum 1/p over p = 9 mod 10, inclusion-exclusion, convergence of sum over squarefull s of 1/s) and the passage from density to b(k)/k.

searched: web search 2026-11-07 (sigma(n) divisible by m for almost all n)
prior_art.note: Follows at once from the classical fact that m | sigma(n) for almost all n; not recorded on the entry.
